messages:
Alex (CS): quick heads-up — Priya from Acme contacted support: after last night's canary->stable flip some nullable/optional keys are being omitted entirely from our structured responses. Their downstream ingest strictly expects those keys (even if null) and is failing. sample below.

Priya (Acme Corp): repro steps:
1) call our inference endpoint with model=redwood-v2.1-canary (worked pre-flip)
2) same prompt + system schema as before
3) see missing keys in json response body (we expect keys 'discount_code' and 'metadata' to be present with nulls).
Curl we used: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.1","input":"Order summary...","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"discount_code":{"type":["string","null"]},"metadata":{"type":["object","null"]}}}}'
```
Response sample BEFORE (last week):
```
{"order_id":"A123","discount_code":null,"metadata":null}
```
Response sample AFTER (post-flip, today):
```
{"order_id":"A123"}
```
This causes our parser to throw KeyError for 'discount_code' since we differentiate between missing key vs explicit null. Can provide logs and full request IDs if needed.

Alex (CS): flagged as P2 for now — customer blocked on a few batch jobs. Can eng check whether the model/serializer changed behavior around omitting nullable keys? Might be related to structured-output heuristic that prunes empty fields to save tokens. @Sophia (ML Eng) any idea?

Sophia (ML Eng): thanks. @Alex (CS) Can you confirm the model version in the header of their failing requests? We need the exact model-tag + rollout id. Also, did they pin a model variant previously?

Priya (Acme Corp): headers attached from one failing request (redacted):
- model: redwood-v2.1
- rollout-id: rollout-2024-11-03-78
- request-id: req-0a1b2c3d
We did not pin; we rely on stable. This started ~2024-11-03 02:15 UTC after your canary promotion.

Alex (CS): adding raw example of our ingest failure: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "ingest_pipeline.py", line 212, in process_record
    discount = record['discount_code']
KeyError: 'discount_code'
```

Mike (Oncall): Deploy Bot shows canary promoted to stable at 2024-11-03T02:10:12Z. Noted.

Deploy Bot: Canary rollout (rollout-2024-11-03-78) -> promoted to stable at 2024-11-03T02:10:12Z. Change list: structured-output-prune-empty-fields=true (opt-in flag turned on globally for stable).

Sophia (ML Eng): aha — that flag is probably the culprit. We had a perf experiment to prune null/empty keys to save tokens for long outputs; it accidentally flipped to true for the stable tier during rollout. We need to assess: 1) does the pruning only omit keys when value is null/empty, 2) can we add a compatibility mode for customers who rely on preserved keys.

Alex (CS): Priya — sorry for the disruption. Two immediate remediation options:
- We can rollback the flag for stable in the next 15-30min (quick but will revert perf gains), or
- Provide a server-side compatibility layer that inserts missing nullable keys as explicit nulls for affected customers (slower; needs dev work).
Which do you prefer?

Priya (Acme Corp): rollback preferred. Our ingestion contracts require those keys to be present. We can accept slight cost/latency delta for now.

Sophia (ML Eng): Roger. @Mike (Oncall) can you push a config rollback for structured-output-prune-empty-fields -> false on stable pool and monitor a few request-ids (req-0a1b2c3d, req-4d5e6f7g) for expected behavior?

Mike (Oncall): executing rollback now. Will watch metrics and APM traces. ETA ~10m.

Deploy Bot: Config change request submitted: change structured-output-prune-empty-fields=false for pool 'stable' (req change-889).

Mike (Oncall): rolled back. Observing logs for replays.

Priya (Acme Corp): re-ran the same request, response now: 
```
{"order_id":"A123","discount_code":null,"metadata":null}
```
Works again. Thank you, team.

Alex (CS): closing loop: action items:
- Sophia/ML: add an opt-out compatibility policy so customers pinned to stable keep keys even if we enable pruning (owner: Sophia, due: 2024-11-10)
- Eng-runtime: add rollout guard so opt-in flags don't flip globally without canary opt-out mapping (owner: Mike, due: 2024-11-07)
- CS: notify other customers who might be impacted and provide rollback offer (owner: Alex, due: 2024-11-04)

Sophia (ML Eng): will open an RFC and a follow-up PR to add a per-tenant compatibility mode.

Alex (CS): Priya — we'll follow up with a formal incident note and a pointer to the request IDs for your audit. Thanks for quick repro and patience. :pray:
